title: Search and Navigation
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of search and navigation and at least two listed subtopics.

content.intro: Learn search and navigation through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Search and Navigation matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines search and navigation as part of localization, accessibility, and user experience. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Server-side search; Filtering and sorting; Empty results; Search pagination; Clear navigation and meaningful URLs. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Server-side search
items.text: Server-side search should be planned for the actual hosting topology: configuration, permissions, resource limits, observability, rollback/recovery and a testable operating procedure all matter.

items.title: Clear navigation and meaningful URLs
items.text: Clear navigation and meaningful URLs shapes the presentation layer. Separate layout from business logic, escape untrusted output, provide meaningful empty/error states, and check semantic structure and keyboard usability.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Search and Navigation
content_blocks.code:
from django.urls import path
from . import views

urlpatterns = [
    path("items/<int:item_id>/", views.item_detail, name="item-detail"),
]
content_blocks.expected_output: The route converter passes an integer item_id to the named view.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Open a local project using the documented Django 6.1-compatible Python environment. If this snippet depends on model names, URL configuration, settings, or an optional package, add those prerequisites before running it. Otherwise inspect it as a static example. CodeLeaf browser preview does not execute Django/Python server code.
content_blocks.troubleshooting: The view and project include() wiring must exist; URL conversion does not perform authorization or database lookup.

content_blocks.text: First identify the input and the responsible Django component. Next trace how the example moves through “Search and Navigation” and the related concept “Server-side search”. content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
